<problem>
Fix an integer \(e\ge 0\). Throughout, \(\mathbb P(V)\) parametrizes one-dimensional complex subspaces of the fibres of a vector bundle \(V\), and \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(V)}(1)\) is the dual of the tautological line subbundle. Let
\[
X=\mathbb P_{\mathbb P^1}\bigl(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e)\bigr),\qquad \pi:X\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1.
\]
Let \(f\) be the divisor class of a fibre of \(\pi\), and let \(S\) be the section defined by the displayed summand \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e)\). Thus \(S^2=-e\), \(S\cdot f=1\), and \(f^2=0\). Set
\[
H=S+(3e+1)f,\qquad P=4H-f,
\]
\[
E_0=\mathcal O_X(5S-f)\oplus\mathcal O_X\bigl(-S+(12e+5)f\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathcal O_X(D)\) denotes the line bundle associated with a divisor \(D\). Write \(\bar\partial_0\) for the split Dolbeault operator of \(E_0\).

Suppose \((\bar\partial_j)_{j\ge1}\) is a sequence of smooth integrable Dolbeault operators on the underlying smooth complex bundle of \(E_0\). Thus \(\bar\partial_j^2=0\). Assume that \(\bar\partial_j-\bar\partial_0\), viewed as an endomorphism-valued \((0,1)\)-form, tends to zero in every finite \(C^m\) norm, measured using fixed smooth background metrics and connections. Let \(E_j\) denote the resulting holomorphic rank-two bundle.

Assume every \(E_j\) is ample and slope-stable with respect to \(P\). Here ampleness means that \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E_j^*)}(1)\) is ample; a line bundle is ample if some positive tensor power has a complete linear system giving a projective embedding. Slope-stability means that every nonzero coherent rank-one subsheaf \(\mathcal F\subset E_j\) satisfies
\[
c_1(\mathcal F)\cdot P<\frac{c_1(E_j)\cdot P}{2},
\]
where \(c_1\) is the first Chern class and the dot denotes intersection on \(X\).

Define the complex fourfolds
\[
U_j=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X\oplus E_j)\setminus\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X),
\]
where the removed section comes from the first summand. For a complex fourfold \(U\), define \(\kappa(U)\) to be the least positive integer \(q\) for which there exist a smooth function \(\psi:U\to\mathbb R\) and a compact subset \(K\subset U\) such that every sublevel set \(\{\psi\le c\}\), for \(c\in\mathbb R\), is compact and the Levi form of \(\psi\) has at least \(5-q\) strictly positive eigenvalues at every point of \(U\setminus K\). The Levi form is the Hermitian form with matrix \((\partial^2\psi/\partial z_a\partial\bar z_b)\) in local holomorphic coordinates.

Determine \(\displaystyle\lim_{j\to\infty}\kappa(U_j)\).
</problem>

A complete answer to this problem: A complete answer must give the exact value of the limit as a function of the fixed integer e≥0, valid for every sequence satisfying the stated hypotheses, and establish that the limit exists. If the value is independent of e and the sequence, the answer is a single positive integer.

11	### The Finsler theorem in the form needed
12	
13	If \(V\) is an ample vector bundle on a projective manifold \(B\) of dimension \(n\), there is a smooth function
14	\[
15	G:V\setminus 0_B\longrightarrow (0,\infty)
16	\]
17	such that
18	\[
19	G(\lambda v)=|\lambda|^2G(v),
20	\]
21	and the Levi form of \(\log G\) has an \(n\)-dimensional negative-definite subspace at every point.
22	
23	This is the consequence of the positive-Finsler-metric theorem that we use. In its usual formulation, \(G\) is a complex Finsler metric with positive Kobayashi curvature: the Levi form of \(\log G\) is negative definite on the Finsler-horizontal subspace.

25	We first prove a general statement.
26	
27	## 1. Upper bound for an ample rank-two bundle on a surface
28	
29	Let \(E\) be an ample rank-two bundle on a smooth projective surface \(X\), and put
30	\[
31	M=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X\oplus E),\qquad
32	Z=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X),\qquad U=M\setminus Z.
33	\]
34	The affine chart where the \(\mathcal O_X\)-coordinate is nonzero is canonically the total space of \(E\), with \(Z\) corresponding to its zero section.
35	
36	Take \(G\) supplied by the Finsler theorem. We claim that
37	\[
38	\phi=\frac1G
39	\]
40	has at least three positive Levi eigenvalues on \(E\setminus 0_X\).
41	
42	Write
43	\[
44	\alpha=\partial\log G,\qquad A=\partial\bar\partial\log G.
45	\]
46	Differentiation gives
47	\[
48	\partial\bar\partial(G^{-1})
49	  =G^{-1}\bigl(-A+\alpha\otimes\overline\alpha\bigr).
50	\tag{1}
51	\]
52	
53	Let \(R=\sum_\nu v^\nu\partial/\partial v^\nu\) be the holomorphic fibrewise Euler vector field. Homogeneity gives
54	\[
55	\alpha(R)=1,\qquad A(R,\overline W)=0
56	\quad\text{for every }W.
57	\tag{2}
58	\]
59	Indeed, \(R(\log G)=1\), and differentiating this equality in an antiholomorphic direction proves the second identity.
60	
61	By the Finsler theorem, \(A\) is negative definite on a complex two-dimensional subspace \(H\). Replace \(H\) by
62	\[
63	H'=\{h-\alpha(h)R:h\in H\}.
64	\]
65	By (2), \(A|_{H'}\) remains negative definite, while \(\alpha|_{H'}=0\). Consequently, on
66	\[
67	H'\oplus\mathbb CR
68	\]
69	the form in parentheses in (1) is positive definite: its first summand is positive on \(H'\), and its second summand is positive on the radial direction. This proves the claim.
70	
71	It remains to make this into a global exhaustion of \(U\). Choose \(\varepsilon>0\) and a smooth function
72	\[
73	\chi:(0,\infty)\longrightarrow[0,\infty)
74	\]
75	equal to \(1/t\) for \(t<\varepsilon\), and equal to \(0\) for \(t>2\varepsilon\). On the punctured affine chart set
76	\[
77	\psi=\chi(G),
78	\]
79	and extend \(\psi\) by zero outside that chart. This is smooth: the set \(G\le 2\varepsilon\) is a bounded disc bundle over the compact base, so the function already vanishes near the boundary of the affine chart.
80	
81	Moreover, \(\psi\to+\infty\) when approaching \(Z\). Since \(M\) is compact, every sublevel set of \(\psi\) is therefore compact in \(U\).
82	
83	The set
84	\[
85	K=M\setminus\bigl(Z\cup\{[1:v]:0<G(v)<\varepsilon\}\bigr)
86	\]
87	is a compact subset of \(U\). Outside \(K\), we have \(\psi=G^{-1}\), whose Levi form has at least three positive eigenvalues. Thus

89	\kappa(U)\le2.
90	\tag{3}
91	\]

93	## 2. A lower bound independent of ampleness
94	
95	In fact, \(\kappa(U)\ge2\) for every rank-two bundle \(E\).
96	
97	Fix \(x\in X\) and trivialize its projective fibre:
98	\[
99	M_x\simeq\mathbb P^2,\qquad Z\cap M_x=\{p\},\qquad p=[1:0:0].
100	\]
101	For real \(t>0\), consider the projective line
102	\[
103	C_t=\{[tu:u:v]:[u:v]\in\mathbb P^1\}.
104	\]
105	It avoids \(p\), so \(C_t\) is a compact holomorphic curve in \(U\). The point
106	\[
107	a_t=[t:1:0]\in C_t
108	\]
109	converges to the removed point \(p\), and hence escapes every compact subset of \(U\).
110	
111	Suppose that an exhaustion \(\psi\) had positive-definite Levi form outside a compact set \(K\). Compactness of its sublevels implies
112	\[
113	\psi(a_t)\longrightarrow+\infty.
114	\]
115	Choose a maximum point \(b_t\) of \(\psi|_{C_t}\). Then
116	\[
117	\psi(b_t)\ge\psi(a_t)\longrightarrow+\infty,
118	\]
119	so \(b_t\notin K\) for all sufficiently large \(t\). But at a maximum on the holomorphic curve \(C_t\),
120	\[
121	\left.\partial\bar\partial\psi\right|_{T_{b_t}C_t}\le0.
122	\]
123	That contradicts positive definiteness of the Levi form at \(b_t\). Therefore
124	\[
125	\kappa(U)\ge2.
126	\tag{4}
127	\]

129	Combining (3) and (4) gives
130	\[
131	\boxed{\kappa\bigl(\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X\oplus E)
132	                   \setminus\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X)\bigr)=2}
133	\]
134	for every ample rank-two bundle on a smooth projective surface. Applying this to each \(E_j\) proves the answer.

145	    "z1 z2 w1 w2 Z1 Z2 W1 W2"
146	)
147	a, d, b, c = s.symbols("a d b c", real=True)
148	
149	z = [z1, z2, w1, w2]
150	zb = [Z1, Z2, W1, W2]

153	Q = (a*z1*Z1 + (b+s.I*c)*z1*Z2

156	phi = 1/G

158	point = {

160	    w1: 1, W1: 1, w2: 0, W2: 0
